2608.18768.title: Readable, Faithful, Used: Three Dissociable Properties of Demographic Identity in a Language Model
2608.18768.paper_summary: Large language models are widely used to simulate survey respondents, yet their answers are homogeneous and unfaithful to real inter-group differences. We ask where demographic group identity lives inside an LLM, how faithfully its geometry mirrors real inter-group opinion structure, and whether it uses what it encodes. Using representational similarity analysis against Pew ground truth over 169 demographic cells, we score 1,089 read-out locations in Mistral-7B and intervene causally across six attribute types. Four results. (1) The standard last-token residual read-out understates the model: attention-head read-outs dominate it in five of six types, with selection-corrected fidelity up to rho=0.63 -- roughly 70% of the measurement-reliability ceiling -- surviving a lexical-similarity control. (2) A single head (L11 H16) is significantly faithful in all six types as a fixed location, while race-based types stay weak and prompt-fragile. Both phenomena replicate -- the analogous head significant in five of six types, weakest on the same race type -- across three checkpoints of a second model family, where ten billion training tokens barely move the map. (3) Causal use does not follow fidelity: the clearest causal pathway sits in one of the least faithful types (p=0.002, cluster-robust, fixed depth), the most faithful type shows no correction-surviving single-layer effect, and replacing the entire identity moves predictions by under 2% of their error. (4) A 128-dimensional probe of the single head lands 21-31% closer to survey truth than the model's own answers -- yet recovers almost none of the per-question group ordering, no better than the answers themselves. Readable, faithfully arranged, and causally used are three dissociable properties of the same model; treating them as one claim is what keeps the "can LLMs simulate populations" debate unresolved.
2608.18768.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型被廣泛用來模擬調查受訪者，但它們的回答是同質的，並且不忠實於真實的群體間差異。我們探討人口群體身份在LLM中的位置、其幾何形狀在多大程度上反映真實的群體意見結構，以及它是否使用其編碼的內容。使用代表性相似性分析對比Pew的真實數據，涵蓋169個人口單元，我們對Mistral-7B中的1,089個讀出位置進行評分，並在六個屬性類型上進行因果干預。四個結果。(1) 標準的最後一個標記殘差讀出低估了模型：在六種類型中，注意力頭讀出在五種類型中佔主導，選擇校正的忠實度高達rho=0.63——大約是測量可靠性上限的70%——在詞彙相似性控制下仍然成立。(2) 單一頭部（L11 H16）在所有六種類型中作為固定位置具有顯著的忠實度，而基於種族的類型則保持弱且對提示脆弱。這兩種現象在第二個模型系列的三個檢查點中重現——類似的頭部在六種類型中有五種類型顯著，對同一種族類型最弱——而十億個訓練標記幾乎沒有改變地圖。(3) 因果使用不遵循忠實度：最清晰的因果路徑位於最不忠實的類型之一（p=0.002，集群穩健，固定深度），最忠實的類型顯示沒有校正存活的單層效應，並且替換整個身份使預測的變化不到其誤差的2%。(4) 單一頭部的128維探針比模型自身的答案更接近調查真相21-31%——但幾乎沒有恢復每個問題的群體排序，效果不比答案本身更好。可讀性、忠實排列和因果使用是同一模型的三個可分離特性；將它們視為一個主張是使「LLMs能否模擬群體」辯論無法解決的原因。
2608.18768.author: Fathin Difa Robbani et.al.
